exposure: presence or absence of postpartum hemorrhage
cohort: 40 patients from 3 German academic hospitals with a diagnosis of pregnancy-related atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (p-aHUS)
finding: Based on the findings, the authors suggest a pragmatic approach toward limited and short-term anticomplement therapy for patients with a clinical diagnosis of p-aHUS, which should be stopped once causes of TMA other than genetic complement abnormalities emerge.
mod_finding: Patients with PPH-associated thrombotic microangiopathy who received complement inhibition experienced partially recovered kidney function.
